text: 3M’s purchases of property, plant and equipment rose from $1,373 million in 2017 to $1,577 million in 2018, an increase of $204 million 204 [3]. text: Coca‑Cola’s net income attributable to shareholders dropped from $6,527 million in 2016 to $1,248 million in 2017, a decline of $5,279 million [2][1]. The decline was driven primarily by a surge in income‑tax expense, which rose to $5,560 million in 2017 from $1,586 million in 2016, raising the effective tax rate to 82.5% from 19.5% [1]. In addition, other income turned into a larger loss of $1,666 million in 2017 versus a $1,234 million loss in 2016, further eroding profit [1]. These tax and other‑income impacts more than offset the modest reductions in SG&A and other operating costs, resulting in the sharp net‑income drop [1].

text: Walmart's consolidated operating income increased by $1,520 million, rising from $20,437 million in fiscal 2018 to $21,957 million in fiscal 2019 [4]. The 10‑K reports that segment operating income grew $391 million in fiscal 2019, with improvements more than offsetting investments in eCommerce, technology, omni‑channel initiatives and higher starting wages [1]. It also cites strong sales performance, productivity improvements and lower operating expense percentages, along with pricing strategy and mix effects from the expanding eCommerce business, as contributors to the higher operating income [2]. These factors together explain the year‑over‑year increase in operating income [1][2].

text: Nike's total revenues increased from $36,397 million in fiscal 2018 to $39,117 million in fiscal 2019, a growth of $2,720 million (about 7%) [7]. The growth was primarily driven by NIKE Direct, whose revenues rose 15% on a reported basis, powered by digital commerce sales up 28%, comparable store sales up 10%, and the opening of new stores [1]. Additional contributions came from higher footwear and apparel sales, with unit sales and higher average selling prices adding roughly three percentage points each to footwear and apparel revenue growth [1]. Overall NIKE Brand revenue also rose 11% on a currency‑neutral basis, supported by strong performance across Greater China, North America, EMEA and APLA regions and the broader Consumer Direct Offense strategy [3].

text: Adobe's total revenue rose from $4,795.5 million in fiscal 2015 to $5,854.4 million in fiscal 2016, an increase of $1,058.9 million, or 22% [1][5]. The company attributes the growth mainly to higher subscription revenue, especially the surge in Creative Cloud subscriptions and related creative offerings, which drove a $873.2 million (38%) increase in Creative revenue [4]. Adobe also cites a $272.7 million (20%) rise in Adobe Marketing Cloud revenue and overall Digital Media ARR growth of $1.13 billion, driven by more paid Creative Cloud and Document Cloud subscriptions and continued ETLA adoption [4][5]. Additionally, the 53‑week fiscal year added an extra week of revenue in the first quarter, contributing to the higher total [1].

text: Block’s total net revenue grew from $4.7 billion in 2019 to $9.5 billion in 2020, an increase of $4.8 billion or 101% year‑over‑year[1]. The surge was driven primarily by a $4.1 billion rise in bitcoin revenue, which accounted for about 85% of the total revenue increase[1]. Additional contributions came from higher subscription and services revenue (+$508 million, 49%) and modest gains in transaction‑based (+$214 million, 7%) and hardware revenue (+$7 million, 8%)[1]. Within the Cash App segment, the $4.9 billion revenue jump was also attributed to growing bitcoin activity, increased Cash App Instant Deposit, Cash Card, Cash for Business usage, and stimulus‑related disbursements[2].
